user: Felix fell off the monkey bars at school yesterday and broke his wrist. How much can we claim from the Meridian policy?
answer:
DearPolicy

I’m sorry Felix was hurt. For Felix, the policy lists S$600 for “Fractured bones (per Accident) — Simple (closed) fracture” and S$1,500 for “Fractured bones (per Accident) — Compound (open) fracture”; the fracture type must be certified in writing by a registered medical practitioner and confirmed by X-ray, and only one of these benefits is payable for the same bone in the same accident. For Felix, “Medical expenses due to Accident (per Accident, reimbursement)” is listed up to S$2,000; the policy requires original bills to support a claim.

A FACT THAT CHANGES THIS ASSESSMENT
Was Felix’s wrist fracture confirmed by X-ray and certified in writing by a registered medical practitioner, and did the broken bone break through the skin?
This changes what your policy pays under: “Items D and E: the type of fracture must be certified in writing by a registered medical practitioner and confirmed by X-ray. Only one of Item D or” (page 1); “4.4 For Items D and E, a Compound fracture means a fracture in which the broken bone breaks through the skin. All” (page 2)

user: I was in hospital after that car accident in March. They admitted me at 9:40pm on 14 March and I was discharged at 8:20am on 18 March. How much hospital cash should Meridian pay me?
answer:
DearPolicy

For your March hospital stay, Meridian’s Hospital daily allowance is S$120 per day for an adult, and the policy counts each complete 24 hours as one day, with a remaining period of 12 hours or more counting as another day (up to 60 days per policy year).

Based on the admission and discharge times you gave, the indicative estimate is S$360 for three payable days; this is not a confirmed payout, assuming at least 3 of the 60 days are still available this policy year.
